children.text: mahimnaḥ pāraṃ te paramaviduṣo yady asadṛśī
stutir brahmādīnām api tadavasannās tvayi giraḥ |
children.translated_text: then the words of even <s>Brahmā</s> and others fall short concerning You;
If praise is unequal to the extent of Your greatness, O Supreme Knower,

children.text: athāvācyaḥ sarvaḥ svamatipariṇāmāvadhi gṛṇan
mamāpy eṣa stotre hara nirapavādaḥ parikaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: this endeavor of mine too in composing this hymn is free from fault, O <s>Hara</s>.
yet since everyone is blameless who praises to the limit of his own understanding,

children.text: mahimnaḥ pāraṃ te paramaviduṣo yady asadṛśī
stutir brahmādīnām api tadavasannās tvayi giraḥ |
atha avācyaḥ sarvaḥ svamatipariṇāmāvadhi gṛṇan
mama apy eṣa stotre hara nirapavādaḥ parikaraḥ ||
atītaḥ panthānaṃ tava ca mahimā vāṅmanasayor
atadvyāvṛttyā yaṃ cakitam abhidhatte śrutir api |
children.translated_text: which even the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) describes with trepidation through negation alone;
Your greatness transcends the path of both speech and mind,

children.text: sa kasya stotavyaḥ katividhaguṇaḥ kasya viṣayaḥ
pade tv arvācīne patati na manaḥ kasya na vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet whose mind and speech do not fall upon the nearer level?
who can praise that? Of how many attributes is it? Whose domain is it?

children.text: atītaḥ panthānaṃ tava ca mahimā vāṅmanasayor
atadvyāvṛttyā yaṃ cakitam abhidhatte śrutir api |
sa kasya stotavyaḥ katividhaguṇaḥ kasya viṣayaḥ
pade tv arvācīne patati na manaḥ kasya na vacaḥ ||
madhusphītā vācaḥ paramam amṛtaṃ nirmitavatas
tava brahman kiṃ vāg api suraguror vismayapadam |
children.translated_text: is even the speech of the preceptor of the gods a cause of wonder?
O <s>Brahman</s>, for You who created the most sweet and supreme nectar-like speech,

children.text: mama tv etāṃ vāṇīṃ guṇakathanapuṇyena bhavataḥ
punāmīty arthe 'smin puramathana buddhir vyavasitā ||
children.translated_text: 'I purify this speech of mine by the merit of narrating Your virtues,' O Destroyer of the Cities.
But as for me, my mind is resolved in this purpose:

children.text: madhusphītā vācaḥ paramam amṛtaṃ nirmitavatas
tava brahman kiṃ vāg api suraguror vismayapadam |
mama tv etāṃ vāṇīṃ guṇakathanapuṇyena bhavataḥ
punāmi ity arthe 'smin puramathana buddhir vyavasitā ||
tavaiśvaryaṃ yat taj jagadudayarakṣāpralayakṛt
trayīvastu vyastaṃ tisṛṣu guṇabhinnāsu tanuṣu |
children.translated_text: is the subject of the three <s>Vedas</s>, distributed in three bodies distinguished by the <s>guṇas</s>;
Your sovereignty, which brings about the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the universe,

children.text: abhavyānām asmin varada ramaṇīyām aramaṇīṃ
vihantuṃ vyākrośīṃ vidadhata ihaike jaḍadhiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeking to destroy this delightful reality, O Bestower of Boons.
some dull-witted ones here fabricate abuse — which is not delightful to the noble —

children.text: tavā eśvaryaṃ yat taj jagadudayarakṣāpralayakṛt
trayīvastu vyastaṃ tisṛṣu guṇabhinnāsu tanuṣu |
abhavyānām asmin varada ramaṇīyām aramaṇīṃ
vihantuṃ vyākrośīṃ vidadhata iha eke jaḍadhiyaḥ ||
kimīhaḥ kiṃkāyaḥ sa khalu kimupāyas tribhuvanaṃ
kimādhāro dhātā sṛjati kimupādāna iti ca |
children.translated_text: What is His support? What is His material cause? — they ask;
What is His desire? What is His body? Who indeed is He? How does He create the three worlds?

children.text: atarkyaiśvarye tvayy anavasaraduḥstho hatadhiyaḥ
kutarko 'yaṃ kāṃścin mukharayati mohāya jagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this sophistry of theirs confounds certain people, deluding the world.
regarding Your lordship, which is beyond logic, those of ruined intellect find no place to rest,

children.text: kimīhaḥ kiṃkāyaḥ sa khalu kimupāyas tribhuvanaṃ
kimādhāro dhātā sṛjati kimupādāna iti ca |
atarkyaiśvarye tvayy anavasaraduḥstho hatadhiyaḥ
kutarko 'yaṃ kāṃścin mukharayati mohāya jagataḥ ||
ajanmāno lokāḥ kim avayavavanto 'pi jagatām
adhiṣṭhātāraṃ kiṃ bhavavidhir anādṛtya bhavati |
children.translated_text: Does the course of existence proceed disregarding a ruler?
Are the worlds unborn? Do the components of the world even exist?

children.text: anīśo vā kuryād bhuvanajanane kaḥ parikaro
yato mandās tvāṃ praty amaravara saṃśerata ime ||
children.translated_text: Thus these dim-witted ones have doubts about You, O Best of the Immortals.
Could a powerless one create the universe? What would be the means?

children.text: ajanmāno lokāḥ kim avayavavanto 'pi jagatām
adhiṣṭhātāraṃ kiṃ bhavavidhir anādṛtya bhavati |
anīśo vā kuryād bhuvanajanane kaḥ parikaro
yato mandās tvāṃ praty amaravara saṃśerata ime ||
trayī sāṃkhyaṃ yogaḥ paśupatimataṃ vaiṣṇavam iti
prabhinne prasthāne param idam adaḥ pathyam iti ca |
children.translated_text: though the paths are diverse, each saying 'this is supreme, that is the way,'
The three <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, the <s>Pāśupata</s> doctrine, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> path —

children.text: rucīnāṃ vaicitryād ṛjukuṭilanānāpathajuṣāṃ
nṛṇām eko gamyas tvam asi payasām arṇava iva ||
children.translated_text: You alone are the destination, as the ocean is for waters.
due to the variety of tastes among people following straight, crooked, and various paths,

children.text: trayī sāṃkhyaṃ yogaḥ paśupatimataṃ vaiṣṇavam iti
prabhinne prasthāne param idam adaḥ pathyam iti ca |
rucīnāṃ vaicitryād ṛjukuṭilanānāpathajuṣāṃ
nṛṇām eko gamyas tvam asi payasām arṇava iva ||
mahokṣaḥ khaṭvāṅgaṃ paraśur ajinaṃ bhasma phaṇinaḥ
kapālaṃ cetīyat tava varada tantropakaraṇam |
children.translated_text: a skull — these, O Bestower of Boons, are Your ritual implements;
A great bull, a skull-topped staff, an axe, a deerskin, ashes, serpents,

children.text: surās tāṃ tām ṛddhiṃ dadhati tu bhavadbhrūpraṇihitāṃ
na hi svātmārāmaṃ viṣayamṛgatṛṣṇā bhramayati ||
children.translated_text: indeed, the mirage of sense-objects does not delude one who delights in the Self.
the gods derive their various powers from the mere movement of Your brow —

children.text: mahokṣaḥ khaṭvāṅgaṃ paraśur ajinaṃ bhasma phaṇinaḥ
kapālaṃ ca iti iyat tava varada tantropakaraṇam |
surās tāṃ tām ṛddhiṃ dadhati tu bhavadbhrūpraṇihitāṃ
na hi svātmārāmaṃ viṣayamṛgatṛṣṇā bhramayati ||
dhruvaṃ kaścit sarvaṃ sakalam aparas tv adhruvam idaṃ
paro dhrauvyādhrauvye jagati gadati vyastaviṣaye |
children.translated_text: yet another speaks of the permanent and impermanent separately in the world;
Some say all this is certainly permanent; another says all this is impermanent;

children.text: samaste 'py etasmin puramathana tair vismita iva
stuvañ jihremi tvāṃ na khalu nanu dhṛṣṭā mukharatā ||
children.translated_text: in praising You I feel ashamed — yet is not bold speech the mark of audacity?
even regarding all of this, O Destroyer of the Cities, as if bewildered by those,

children.text: dhruvaṃ kaścit sarvaṃ sakalam aparas tv adhruvam idaṃ
paro dhrauvyādhrauvye jagati gadati vyastaviṣaye |
samaste 'py etasmin puramathana tair vismita iva
stuvañ jihremi tvāṃ na khalu nanu dhṛṣṭā mukharatā ||
tavaiśvaryaṃ yatnād yad upari viriñco harir adhaḥ
paricchettuṃ yātāv analam analaskandhavapuṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: went to ascertain the limits of, You whose body was a column of fire —
Your sovereignty — that which <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) above and <s>Hari</s> below

children.text: tato bhaktiśraddhābharagurugṛṇadbhyāṃ giriśa yat
svayaṃ tasthe tābhyāṃ tava kim anuvṛttir na phalati ||
children.translated_text: does not devotion to You bear fruit?
then, O Lord of Mountains, when You stood revealed of Your own accord to them both, who praised You weighed down by devotion and faith,

children.text: tavā eśvaryaṃ yatnād yad upari viriñco harir adhaḥ
paricchettuṃ yātāv analam analaskandhavapuṣaḥ |
tato bhaktiśraddhābharagurugṛṇadbhyāṃ giriśa yat
svayaṃ tasthe tābhyāṃ tava kim anuvṛttir na phalati ||
ayatnād āpādya tribhuvanam avairavyatikaraṃ
daśāsyo yad bāhūn abhṛta raṇakaṇḍūparavaśān |
children.translated_text: lifted his arms, overcome by the itch of battle —
When the ten-headed one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), who had effortlessly brought the three worlds to a state free from enmity,

children.text: śiraḥpadmaśreṇīracitacaraṇāmbhoruhabaleḥ
sthirāyās tvadbhaktes tripurahara visphūrjitam idam ||
children.translated_text: this outburst was from his firm devotion to You, O Destroyer of the Three Cities.
his lotus-feet worshipped with rows of lotus-heads —

children.text: ayatnād āpādya tribhuvanam avairavyatikaraṃ
daśāsyo yad bāhūn abhṛta raṇakaṇḍūparavaśān |
śiraḥpadmaśreṇīracitacaraṇāmbhoruhabaleḥ
sthirāyās tvadbhaktes tripurahara visphūrjitam idam ||
amuṣya tvatsevāsamadhigatasāraṃ bhujavanaṃ
balāt kailāse 'pi tvadadhivasatau vikramayataḥ |
children.translated_text: tried by force to shake even <s>Kailāsa</s>, Your abode —
When he whose forest of arms had attained its essence through service to You

children.text: alabhyā pātāle 'py alasacalitāṅguṣṭhaśirasi
pratiṣṭhā tvayy āsīd dhruvam upacito muhyati khalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely the wicked one who is puffed up becomes deluded.
stability unattainable even in the netherworld was his, when the tip of Your casually moved great toe pressed upon his head —

children.text: amuṣya tvatsevāsamadhigatasāraṃ bhujavanaṃ
balāt kailāse 'pi tvadadhivasatau vikramayataḥ |
alabhyā pātāle 'py alasacalitāṅguṣṭhaśirasi
pratiṣṭhā tvayy āsīd dhruvam upacito muhyati khalaḥ ||
yadṛddhiṃ sutrāmṇo varada paramoccair api satīm
adhaś cakre bāṇaḥ parijanavidheyatribhuvanaḥ |
children.translated_text: even the very high glory of <s>Indra</s>, O Bestower of Boons —
When <s>Bāṇa</s>, who had the three worlds obedient as his retinue, brought down

children.text: na tac citraṃ tasmin varivasitari tvaccaraṇayor
na kasyā unnatyai bhavati śirasas tvayy avanatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for whose bowing of the head before You does not lead to exaltation?
that is no wonder, for he worshipped Your feet;

children.text: yadṛddhiṃ sutrāmṇo varada paramoccair api satīm
adhaś cakre bāṇaḥ parijanavidheyatribhuvanaḥ |
na tac citraṃ tasmin varivasitari tvaccaraṇayor
na kasyā unnatyai bhavati śirasas tvayy avanatiḥ ||
akāṇḍabrahmāṇḍakṣayacakitadevāsurakṛpā
vidheyasyāsīd yas trinayana viṣaṃ saṃhṛtavataḥ |
children.translated_text: who consumed the poison, O Three-Eyed One —
You who had compassion on the gods and <s>Asuras</s> terrified by the untimely destruction of the universe,

children.text: na kalmāṣaḥ kaṇṭhe tava na kurute na śriyam aho
vikāro 'pi ślāghyo bhuvananbhayabhaṅgavyasaninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even a blemish is praiseworthy in one devoted to dispelling the fear of the world!
the dark stain on Your throat does not diminish but rather adds to Your beauty; ah,

children.text: akāṇḍabrahmāṇḍakṣayacakitadevāsurakṛpā
vidheyasyā asīd yas trinayana viṣaṃ saṃhṛtavataḥ |
na kalmāṣaḥ kaṇṭhe tava na kurute na śriyam aho
vikāro 'pi ślāghyo bhuvananbhayabhaṅgavyasaninaḥ ||
asiddhārthā naiva kvacid api sadevāsuranare
nivartante nityaṃ jagati jayino yasya viśikhāḥ |
children.translated_text: who is always victorious —
He whose arrows are never unsuccessful anywhere in the world of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and men,

children.text: sa paśyan īśa tvām itarasurasādhāraṇam abhūt
smaraḥ smartavyātmā na hi vaśiṣu pathyaḥ paribhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love), who is to be remembered in bodiless form — for insult is not wholesome for the self-controlled.
even he, seeing You, O Lord, became equal to other ordinary gods;

children.text: asiddhārthā na eva kvacid api sadevāsuranare
nivartante nityaṃ jagati jayino yasya viśikhāḥ |
sa paśyan īśa tvām itarasurasādhāraṇam abhūt
smaraḥ smartavyātmā na hi vaśiṣu pathyaḥ paribhavaḥ ||
mahī pādāghātād vrajati sahasā saṃśayapadaṃ
padaṃ viṣṇor bhrāmyadbhujaparigharugṇagrahagaṇam |
children.translated_text: the realm of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, its planetary hosts shattered by the battering of Your whirling arms;
The earth suddenly reaches a precarious state from the stamping of Your feet;

children.text: muhur dyaur dauḥsthyaṃ yāty anibhṛtajaṭātāḍitataṭā
jagadrakṣāyai tvaṃ naṭasi nanu vāmaiva vibhutā ||
children.translated_text: You dance for the protection of the world; truly, even destructive power can be gracious!
the sky repeatedly falls into distress, its edges struck by Your swaying matted locks —

children.text: mahī pādāghātād vrajati sahasā saṃśayapadaṃ
padaṃ viṣṇor bhrāmyadbhujaparigharugṇagrahagaṇam |
muhur dyaur dauḥsthyaṃ yāty anibhṛtajaṭātāḍitataṭā
jagadrakṣāyai tvaṃ naṭasi nanu vāma aiva vibhutā ||
viyadvyāpī tārāgaṇaguṇitaphenodgamaruciḥ
pravāho vārāṃ yaḥ pṛṣ.atalaghudṛṣṭaḥ śirasi te |
children.translated_text: appears as light as a droplet upon Your head;
The stream of waters that pervades the sky, its foam-crests beautified by clusters of stars,

children.text: jagad dvīpākāraṃ jaladhivalayaṃ tena kṛtam ity
anenaivonneyaṃ dhṛtamahima divyaṃ tava vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: from this alone the magnitude of Your divine body, which sustains great glory, may be inferred.
by this the world appears like an island-continent encircled by the ocean —

children.text: viyadvyāpī tārāgaṇaguṇitaphenodgamaruciḥ
pravāho vārāṃ yaḥ pṛṣ.atalaghudṛṣṭaḥ śirasi te |
jagad dvīpākāraṃ jaladhivalayaṃ tena kṛtam ity
anena eva unneyaṃ dhṛtamahima divyaṃ tava vapuḥ ||
rathaḥ kṣoṇī yantā śatadhṛtir agendro dhanur atho
rathāṅge candrārkau rathacaraṇapāṇiḥ śara iti |
children.translated_text: the sun and moon the chariot-wheels, <s>Viṣṇu</s> the arrow —
The earth was the chariot, the Hundred-Yoked One (<s>Brahmā</s>) the charioteer, Mount <s>Meru</s> the bow,

children.text: didhakṣos te ko 'yaṃ tripuratṛṇam āḍambaravidhir
vidheyaiḥ krīḍantyo na khalu paratantrāḥ prabhudhiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are sovereign play with their instruments; they are not truly dependent on them.
what was this grand display for You who wished to burn the three cities, mere straw?

children.text: rathaḥ kṣoṇī yantā śatadhṛtir agendro dhanur atho
rathāṅge candrārkau rathacaraṇapāṇiḥ śara iti |
didhakṣos te ko 'yaṃ tripuratṛṇam āḍambaravidhir
vidheyaiḥ krīḍantyo na khalu paratantrāḥ prabhudhiyaḥ ||
haris te sāhasraṃ kamalabalim ādhāya padayor
yad ekone tasmin nijam udaharan netrakamalam |
children.translated_text: when he found one missing, plucked out his own lotus-eye;
<s>Hari</s>, having placed a thousand lotus offerings at Your feet,

children.text: gato bhaktyudrekaḥ pariṇatim asau cakravapuṣā
trayāṇāṃ rakṣāyai tripurahara jāgarti jagatām ||
children.translated_text: for the protection of the three worlds, O Destroyer of the Three Cities, he keeps vigil.
his devotion, having reached its culmination, transformed into the form of the discus —

children.text: haris te sāhasraṃ kamalabalim ādhāya padayor
yad ekone tasmin nijam udaharan netrakamalam |
gato bhaktyudrekaḥ pariṇatim asau cakravapuṣā
trayāṇāṃ rakṣāyai tripurahara jāgarti jagatām ||
kratau supte jāgrat tvam asi phalayoge kratumatāṃ
kva karma pradhvastaṃ palati puruṣārādhanam ṛte |
children.translated_text: where would the destroyed ritual go without the worship of the Supreme Person?
When the sacrifice sleeps, You are awake for bestowing its fruit upon the sacrificers;

children.text: atas tvāṃ samprekṣya tratuṣu phaladānapratibhuvaṃ
śrutau śraddhāṃ baddhvā dṛḍhaparikaraḥ karmasu janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: people, binding their faith in the <s>Vedas</s>, engage in rituals with firm resolve.
Therefore, seeing You as the guarantor of fruit in sacrifices,

children.text: kratau supte jāgrat tvam asi phalayoge kratumatāṃ
kva karma pradhvastaṃ palati puruṣārādhanam ṛte |
atas tvāṃ samprekṣya tratuṣu phaladānapratibhuvaṃ
śrutau śraddhāṃ baddhvā dṛḍhaparikaraḥ karmasu janaḥ ||
kriyādakṣo dakṣaḥ kratupatir adhīśas tanubhṛtām
ṛṣīṇām ārtvijyaṃ śaraṇada sadasyāḥ suragaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: the hosts of sages were the priests, the hosts of gods the assembly, O Giver of Refuge;
<s>Dakṣa</s>, skilled in ritual, was the lord of sacrifice and the ruler of embodied beings;

children.text: kratubhraṃśas tvattaḥ kratuphalavidhānavyasanino
dhruvaṃ kartuḥ śraddhāvidhuram abhicārāya hi makhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: rituals surely become a means of destruction when performed without faith in the doer.
the destruction of the sacrifice came from You — for the one obsessed with administering the fruits of sacrifice,

children.text: kriyādakṣo dakṣaḥ kratupatir adhīśas tanubhṛtām
ṛṣīṇām ārtvijyaṃ śaraṇada sadasyāḥ suragaṇāḥ |
kratubhraṃśas tvattaḥ kratuphalavidhānavyasanino
dhruvaṃ kartuḥ śraddhāvidhuram abhicārāya hi makhāḥ ||
prajānāthaṃ prasabham abhikaṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ
gataṃ rohidbhūtāṃ riramayiṣum ṛśyasya vapuṣā |
children.translated_text: who had taken the form of a doe, seeking to sport with her in the body of a stag —
When the Lord of Creatures (<s>Prajāpati</s>), overcome by desire, pursued his own daughter

children.text: dhanuṣpāṇer yātaṃ divam api sapatrākṛtam amuṃ
trasantaṃ te 'dyāpi tyajati na mṛgavyādharabhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: trembling — even today Your fury as the Hunter (<s>Mṛgavyādha</s>) does not abandon him.
him whom You pursued, bow in hand, even into heaven, rendering him winged like a hunted bird,

children.text: prajānāthaṃ prasabham abhikaṃ svāṃ duhitaraṃ
gataṃ rohidbhūtāṃ riramayiṣum ṛśyasya vapuṣā |
dhanuṣpāṇer yātaṃ divam api sapatrākṛtam amuṃ
trasantaṃ te 'dya api tyajati na mṛgavyādharabhasaḥ ||
svalāvaṇyāśaṃsādhṛtadhanuṣam ahnāya tṛṇavat
puraḥ pluṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā puramathana puṣpāyudham api |
children.translated_text: burned like mere straw in an instant before You, O Destroyer of the Cities —
Having seen even the Flower-Armed One (<s>Kāma</s>), who wielded his bow proud of his own beauty,

children.text: yadi straiṇaṃ yamanirata dehārdhaghaṭanād
avaiti tvām addhā bata varada mugdhā yuvatayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then alas, O Bestower of Boons, truly those maidens are deluded!
if young women consider You susceptible to the feminine, due to Your union with the half-body of a woman (<s>Umā</s>),

children.text: svalāvaṇyāśaṃsādhṛtadhanuṣam ahnāya tṛṇavat
puraḥ pluṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā puramathana puṣpāyudham api |
yadi straiṇaṃ yamanirata dehārdhaghaṭanād
avaiti tvām addhā bata varada mugdhā yuvatayaḥ ||
śmaśāneṣv ākrīḍā smarahara piśācāḥ sahacarāś
citābhasmālepaḥ srag api nṛkaroṭīparikaraḥ |
children.translated_text: the smearing of funeral pyre ashes, and even garlands with a necklace of human skulls —
Cremation grounds are Your playground, O Destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>; ghosts and goblins are Your companions;

children.text: amāṅgalyaṃ śīlaṃ tava bhavatu nāmaivam akhilaṃ
tathāpi smart.Rṇāṃ varada paramaṃ maṅgalam asi ||
children.translated_text: yet even so, O Bestower of Boons, You are the supreme auspiciousness for those who remember You.
Your conduct may be entirely inauspicious in name,

children.text: śmaśāneṣv ākrīḍā smarahara piśācāḥ sahacarāś
citābhasmālepaḥ srag api nṛkaroṭīparikaraḥ |
amāṅgalyaṃ śīlaṃ tava bhavatu nāma evam akhilaṃ
tatha āpi smart.Rṇāṃ varada paramaṃ maṅgalam asi ||
manaḥ pratyakcitte savidham avadhāyāttamarutaḥ
prahṛṣyadromāṇaḥ pramadasalilotsaṅgitadṛśaḥ |
children.translated_text: with hair standing on end, with eyes brimming with tears of bliss —
Having fixed the mind inward upon the consciousness, with breath controlled,

children.text: yad ālokyāhlādaṃ hrada iva nimajyāmṛtamaye
dadhaty antas tattvaṃ kim api yaminas tat kila bhavān ||
children.translated_text: the <s>yogins</s> hold within themselves some ineffable truth — that, indeed, is You.
when they behold and plunge into joy as into a pool of nectar,

children.text: manaḥ pratyak-citte savidham avadhāyā attamarutaḥ
prahṛṣyadromāṇaḥ pramadasalilotsaṅgitadṛśaḥ |
yad ālokyā ahlādaṃ hrada iva nimajya amṛtamaye
dadhaty antas tattvaṃ kim api yaminas tat kila bhavān ||
tvam arkas tvaṃ somas tvam asi pavanas tvaṃ hutavahas
tvam āpas tvaṃ vyoma tvam u dharaṇir ātmā tvam iti ca |
children.translated_text: You are water, You are space, You are the earth, and You are the Self — thus they say;
You are the sun, You are the moon, You are the wind, You are fire,

children.text: paricchinnām evaṃ tvayi pariṇatā bibhrati giraṃ
na vidmas tat tattvaṃ vayam iha tu yat tvaṃ na bhavasi ||
children.translated_text: we do not know what reality there is that You are not.
though people utter this speech of limited description about You,

children.text: tvam arkas tvaṃ somas tvam asi pavanas tvaṃ hutavahas
tvam āpas tvaṃ vyoma tvam u dharaṇir ātmā tvam iti ca |
paricchinnām evaṃ tvayi pariṇatā bibhrati giraṃ
na vidmas tat tattvaṃ vayam iha tu yat tvaṃ na bhavasi ||
trayīṃ tisro vṛttīs tribhuvanam atho trīn api surān
nakārādyair varṇais tribhir abhidadhat tīrṇavikṛti |
children.translated_text: O Shelter-Giver, transcending all modification;
The syllable <s>OṂ</s>, by its three constituent sounds, denotes the three <s>Vedas</s>, the three states of being, the three worlds, and the three gods,

children.text: turīyaṃ te dhāma dhvanibhir avarundhānam aṇubhiḥ
samastaṃ vyastaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇada gṛṇātīm iti padam ||
children.translated_text: the syllable <s>OṂ</s> praises You both in aggregate and separately.
Your fourth state (<s>turīya</s>), apprehended by the subtle sounds,

children.text: trayīṃ tisro vṛttīs tribhuvanam atho trīn api surān
nakārādyair varṇais tribhir abhidadhat tīrṇavikṛti |
turīyaṃ te dhāma dhvanibhir avarundhānam aṇubhiḥ
samastaṃ vyastaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇada gṛṇāti im iti padam ||
bhavaḥ śarvo rudraḥ paśupatir athograḥ sahamahāṃs
tathā bhīmeśānāv iti yad abhidhānāṣṭakam idam |
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> — this is the eightfold designation;
<s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, and <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Sahamahān</s>,

children.text: amuṣmin pratyekaṃ pravicarati deva śrutir api
priyāyāsmai dhāmne praṇihitanamasyo 'smi bhavate ||
children.translated_text: to this beloved form of Yours I am bowed in reverence.
upon each of these, O God, the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) elaborates;

children.text: bhavaḥ śarvo rudraḥ paśupatir atha ugraḥ sahamahāṃs
tathā bhīmeśānāv iti yad abhidhānāṣṭakam idam |
amuṣmin pratyekaṃ pravicarati deva śrutir api
priyāya asmai dhāmne praṇihitanamasyo 'smi bhavate ||
namo nediṣṭhāya priyadava daviṣṭhāya ca namo
namaḥ kṣodiṣṭhāya smarahara mahiṣṭhāya ca namaḥ |
children.translated_text: Homage to the Smallest, O Destroyer of <s>Kāma</s>, and homage to the Greatest!
Homage to the Nearest, O Lover of the forest, and homage to the Farthest!

children.text: namo varṣiṣṭhāya trinayana yaviṣṭhāya ca namo
namaḥ sarvasmai te tad idam iti sarvāya ca namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to You who are everything, and homage to You who are this — that is, to the All!
Homage to the Eldest, O Three-Eyed One, and homage to the Youngest!

children.text: namo nediṣṭhāya priyadava daviṣṭhāya ca namo
namaḥ kṣodiṣṭhāya smarahara mahiṣṭhāya ca namaḥ |
namo varṣiṣṭhāya trinayana yaviṣṭhāya ca namo
namaḥ sarvasmai te tad idam iti sarvāya ca namaḥ ||
bahularajase viśvotpattau bhavāya namo namaḥ
prabalatamase tatsaṃhāre harāya namo namaḥ |
children.translated_text: To <s>Hara</s>, of prevailing <s>tamas</s> (darkness), in its dissolution — homage, homage!
To <s>Bhava</s>, of abundant <s>rajas</s> (passion), in the creation of the universe — homage, homage!

children.text: janasukhakṛte sattvotpattau mṛdāya namo namaḥ
pramahasi pade nistraiguṇye śivāya namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Śiva</s>, in the luminous state beyond the three <s>guṇas</s> — homage, homage!
To <s>Mṛḍa</s>, who creates happiness for beings, in the arising of <s>sattva</s> (goodness) — homage, homage!

children.text: bahularajase viśvotpattau bhavāya namo namaḥ
prabalatamase tatsaṃhāre harāya namo namaḥ |
janasukhakṛte sattvotpattau mṛdāya namo namaḥ
pramahasi pade nistraiguṇye śivāya namo namaḥ ||
kṛśapariṇati cetaḥ kleśavaśyaṃ kva cedaṃ
kva ca tava guṇasīmollaṅghinī śāśvadṛddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: and where is Your eternally flourishing glory that transcends the bounds of virtues!
Where is this mind of mine, of meager capacity, subject to the afflictions of the heart,

children.text: iti cakitam anandīkṛtya māṃ bhaktir ādhād
varaca caraṇayos te vākyapuṣpopahāram ||
children.translated_text: has placed at Your feet, O Excellent One, this offering of flowers in the form of words.
Yet devotion, having first made me hesitant and then emboldened me,

children.text: kṛśapariṇati cetaḥ kleśavaśyaṃ kva ca idaṃ
kva ca tava guṇasīmollaṅghinī śāśvadṛddhiḥ |
iti cakitam anandīkṛtya māṃ bhaktir ādhād
varaca caraṇayos te vākyapuṣpopahāram ||
pariśiṣṭam: Additional verses in all MSS (!!) but not in the inscription
asitagirisamaṃ syāt kajjalaṃ sindhupātre
surataruvaraśākhā lekhanī patram urvī |
children.translated_text: with the foremost branch of the wish-fulfilling tree as a pen and the earth as the writing surface,
If there were ink equal to a dark mountain in a vessel the size of the ocean,

children.text: likhati yadi gṛhītvā śāradā sarvakālaṃ
tad api tava guṇānām īśa pāraṃ na yāti ||
children.translated_text: even that does not reach the limit of Your qualities, O Lord.
if <s>Śāradā</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>, goddess of learning) were to write for all time —

children.text: asitagirisamaṃ syāt kajjalaṃ sindhupātre
surataruvaraśākhā lekhanī patram urvī |
likhati yadi gṛhītvā śāradā sarvakālaṃ
tad api tava guṇānām īśa pāraṃ na yāti ||
asurasuramunīndrair arcitasyendumauleḥ
prathitaguṇamahimno nirguṇasyeśvarasya |
children.translated_text: whose greatness of qualities is celebrated, who is beyond qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), the Supreme Lord —
Of Him who is worshipped by <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Suras</s>, and lords of sages, who bears the moon as His crest,

children.text: sakalaguṇavariṣṭhaḥ puṣpadantābhidhāno
ruciram alaghuvṛttaiḥ stotram etac cakāra ||
children.translated_text: composed this hymn (<s>stotra</s>) in beautiful verses of considerable weight.
the one named <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, foremost in all virtues,

children.text: asurasuramunīndrair arcitasya indumauleḥ
prathitaguṇamahimno nirguṇasyā iśvarasya |
sakalaguṇavariṣṭhaḥ puṣpadantābhidhāno
ruciram alaghuvṛttaiḥ stotram etac cakāra ||
aharāhar anavadyaṃ dhūrjaṭe stotram etat
paṭhati paramabhaktyā śuddhacittaḥ pumān yaḥ |
children.translated_text: whoever recites it with supreme devotion and a pure mind —
Day after day, this faultless hymn to <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: sa bhavati śivaloke rudratulyaḥ sadātmā
pracurataradhanāyuḥ putravān kīrtimāṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: with abundant wealth and long life, blessed with sons and fame.
he abides in <s>Śiva</s>'s world, equal to <s>Rudra</s>, ever-souled,

children.text: ahara ahar anavadyaṃ dhūrjaṭe stotram etat
paṭhati paramabhaktyā śuddhacittaḥ pumān yaḥ |
sa bhavati śivaloke rudratulyaḥ sadātmā
pracurataradhanāyuḥ putravān kīrtimāṃś ca ||
maheśān nāparo devo mahimno nāparā stutiḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no god other than <s>Maheśa</s>; there is no hymn other than the <s>Mahimna</s> (<s>stotra</s>);

children.text: aghorān nāparo mantro nāsti tattvaṃ guroḥ param ||
children.translated_text: there is no <s>mantra</s> other than the <s>Aghora</s>; there is no truth higher than the <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: maheśān na aparo devo mahimno na aparā stutiḥ |
aghorān na aparo mantro na asti tattvaṃ guroḥ param ||
dīkṣā dānaṃ tapas tīrthaṃ jñānaṃ yāgādikāḥ kriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), charity (<s>dāna</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), pilgrimage (<s>tīrtha</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), sacrificial rites (<s>yāga</s>), and other practices —

children.text: mahimnas tava pāṭhasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: these do not equal even a sixteenth part of the recitation of Your <s>Mahimna</s>.

children.text: dīkṣā dānaṃ tapas tīrthaṃ jñānaṃ yāgādikāḥ kriyāḥ |
mahimnas tava pāṭhasya kalāṃ na arhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
āsamāptam idaṃ stotraṃ puṇyaṃ gandharvabhāṣitam |
children.translated_text: This complete hymn, holy and spoken by the <s>Gandharva</s>,

children.text: anaupamyaṃ manohāri śivam īśvaravarṇanam ||
children.translated_text: incomparable, captivating the heart — a description of the auspicious Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).

children.text: āsamāptam idaṃ stotraṃ puṇyaṃ gandharvabhāṣitam |
anaupamyaṃ manohāri śivam īśvaravarṇanam ||
kusumadaśananāmā sarvagandharvarājaḥ
śiśuśaśadharamauler devadevasya dāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: a servant of the God of Gods (<s>Devadeva</s>) whose crest bears the young moon —
<s>Kusumadaśana</s> ('Flower-tooth') by name, king of all <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: sa khalu nijamahimno bhraṣṭa evāsya roṣāt
stavanam idam akārṣīd divyadivyaṃ mahimnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: composed this supremely divine hymn of praise to His greatness (<s>Mahimna</s>).
he, having indeed fallen from his own greatness by His wrath,

children.text: kusumadaśananāmā sarvagandharvarājaḥ
śiśuśaśadharamauler devadevasya dāsaḥ |
sa khalu nijamahimno bhraṣṭa eva asya roṣāt
stavanam idam akārṣīd divyadivyaṃ mahimnaḥ ||
suragurum abhipūjya svargamokṣaikahetuṃ
paṭhati yadi manuṣyaḥ prāñjalir nānyacetāḥ |
children.translated_text: if a person recites [this hymn] with folded hands and undistracted mind,
Having worshipped the <s>Guru</s> of the gods, the sole cause of heaven and liberation,

children.text: vrajati śivasamīpaṃ kinnaraiḥ stūyamānaḥ
stavanam idam amoghaṃ puṣpadantapraṇītam ||
children.translated_text: this unfailing hymn was composed by <s>Puṣpadanta</s>.
he goes to the presence of <s>Śiva</s>, praised by <s>Kinnaras</s> —

children.text: suragurum abhipūjya svargamokṣaikahetuṃ
paṭhati yadi manuṣyaḥ prāñjalir na anyacetāḥ |
vrajati śivasamīpaṃ kinnaraiḥ stūyamānaḥ
stavanam idam amoghaṃ puṣpadantapraṇītam ||
śrīpuṣpadantamukhapaṅkajanirgatena stotreṇa kilbiṣahareṇa harapriyeṇa |
children.translated_text: By this hymn, born from the lotus-face of the glorious <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, which destroys sins and is dear to <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: kaṇṭhasthitena paṭhitena gṛhasthitena samprīṇito bhavati bhūtapatir maheśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether held in the throat (memorized), recited, or kept in the house — the Lord of beings, <s>Maheśa</s>, is fully pleased.

children.text: śrīpuṣpadantamukhapaṅkajanirgatena stotreṇa kilbiṣahareṇa harapriyeṇa |
kaṇṭhasthitena paṭhitena gṛhasthitena samprīṇito bhavati bhūtapatir maheśaḥ ||
apūrvaṃ lāvaṇyaṃ vivasanatanos te vimṛṣatāṃ
munīnāṃ dārāṇāṃ samajani sa ko 'py avyatikaraḥ |
children.translated_text: there arose some inexplicable confusion among their wives.
When the sages contemplated the unprecedented beauty of Your naked body,

children.text: yato bhagne guhye sakṛd api saparyāṃ vidadhatāṃ
dhruvaṃ mokṣaṃ līlāṃ kim api puruṣārthaṃ prasavite ||
children.translated_text: surely attain liberation — [that organ] effortlessly bestows some purpose of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).
Since, when the secret (<s>liṅga</s>) was broken, those who worship it even once

children.text: apūrvaṃ lāvaṇyaṃ vivasanatanos te vimṛṣatāṃ
munīnāṃ dārāṇāṃ samajani sa ko 'py avyatikaraḥ |
yato bhagne guhye sakṛd api saparyāṃ vidadhatāṃ
dhruvaṃ mokṣaṃ līlāṃ kim api puruṣārthaṃ prasavite ||
vapuḥprādurbhāvād anumitam idaṃ janmani purā
purāre naivāhaṃ kvacid api bhavantaṃ praṇatavān |
children.translated_text: O Destroyer of <s>Pura</s> (<s>Tripura</s>), I never bowed to You anywhere before.
Because Your bodily manifestation was not known to me in a previous birth,

children.text: naman muktaḥ sampraty atanur aham agre 'py anatimān
maheśa kṣantavyaṃ tad idam aparādhadvayam api ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Maheśa</s>, may this twofold offense be forgiven.
Bowing now, I am freed; bodiless [in the future], I shall again not bow — being without a body.

children.text: vapuḥprādurbhāvād anumitam idaṃ janmani purā
purāre na eva ahaṃ kvacid api bhavantaṃ praṇatavān |
naman muktaḥ sampraty atanur aham agre 'py anatimān
maheśa kṣantavyaṃ tad idam aparādhadvayam api ||
ity eṣā vāṅmayī pūjā śrīmacchaṃkarapādayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus this verbal worship at the feet of the glorious <s>Śaṃkara</s>

children.text: arpitā tena deveśaḥ prīyatāṃ me sadāśivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is offered; may the Lord of Gods, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, be pleased with me.

children.text: ity eṣā vāṅmayī pūjā śrīmacchaṃkarapādayoḥ |
arpitā tena deveśaḥ prīyatāṃ me sadāśivaḥ ||
tava tattvaṃ na jānāmi kīdṛśo 'si maheśvara |
children.translated_text: I do not know Your true nature — what You are like, O <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: yādṛśo 'si mahādeva tādṛśāya namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever You are, O <s>Mahādeva</s> — to that [form] I bow again and again.

children.text: tava tattvaṃ na jānāmi kīdṛśo 'si maheśvara |
yādṛśo 'si mahādeva tādṛśāya namo namaḥ ||
ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ yaḥ paṭhen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A person who recites [this] once, twice, or three times a day,

children.text: lambapāśavinirmuktaḥ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: freed from the noose of death, goes to <s>Śiva</s>'s world.

children.text: ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ yaḥ paṭhen naraḥ |
lambapāśavinirmuktaḥ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
kīrtanena hi rudrasya pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā |
children.translated_text: By the glorification of <s>Rudra</s>, sin is dispersed a thousandfold,

children.text: pracaṇḍapavanenaiva dhanaṃ jaladamaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: as a mass of clouds [is dispersed] by a fierce wind.

children.text: kīrtanena hi rudrasya pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā |
pracaṇḍapavanena eva dhanaṃ jaladamaṇḍalam ||
